spec.headline: Deer on the road? Know which coverage helps

entries.caption:
It's deer season on Northwest roads, and dusk comes early now. If one darts out in front of you, which part of your policy steps in? 🦌

Hitting an animal is usually handled under comprehensive coverage, not collision. That matters because the two often carry different deductibles, and comprehensive is optional, so it's only there if it's on your policy.

A few things to keep in mind:
• If you swerve to miss the deer and hit a guardrail or another car, that's often treated as a collision instead
• Liability-only policies generally don't cover damage to your own car either way
• Slowing down at dawn and dusk on wooded roads is still the best protection

Not sure whether you carry comprehensive? Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com and we'll walk through it.

Coverage varies by policy, state and eligibility.

spec.headline: Who's listed as your life insurance beneficiary?
points: Check it after big life changes
Your will may not override it

entries.caption:
Quick question before the family gathers this week: do you know who's named as the beneficiary on your life insurance? 💡

The beneficiary is the person (or people) who would receive the policy's benefit. It's easy to set once and forget, but life changes. A marriage, divorce, new baby or a loss in the family are all good reasons to take a fresh look.

A few basics:
• A primary beneficiary is first in line; a contingent beneficiary is the backup
• Beneficiary designations are generally separate from your will, so updating one doesn't automatically update the other
• Group life through work has its own beneficiary form, too

This post is educational only. Want help understanding your options? Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com.

Coverage, features and availability vary by policy, state and eligibility.

spec.headline: Thanksgiving: the No. 1 day for home cooking fires

entries.caption:
Thanksgiving is the peak day of the year for home cooking fires, according to the National Fire Protection Association. A busy stovetop and a full house can be a risky mix. 🦃

Fire is generally one of the core perils a homeowners policy is built for. Depending on your policy, it can help with:
• Repairs to your home's structure (dwelling coverage)
• Damaged belongings, like furniture, dishes and small appliances (personal property)
• A place to stay if the kitchen is unusable (loss of use)

A few habits help keep the day on track: stay in the kitchen while frying or boiling, keep towels and packaging away from burners, and know where your extinguisher is. A lid slid over a small pan fire can smother it.

Questions about how your home policy handles fire? Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com.

Coverage varies by policy, state and eligibility.

spec.headline: Stocked up for the holidays? Check your limits
points: Limits are set by what you report

entries.caption:
Busy season means fuller shelves. If something happened to your shop this week, would your coverage keep up with all that extra stock? 🛍️

Business property coverage, often part of a business owner's policy (BOP), helps protect things like inventory, equipment and fixtures. The limit is usually based on the values you report, and many businesses set it when stock is at a normal level.

That's why the holidays can create a gap:
• Inventory may be well above your usual amount
• Your limit may not reflect that peak
• Some policies offer options for seasonal increases, depending on the policy and eligibility

It's worth a quick look before the rush hits full speed. Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com to talk through your business coverage.

Coverage varies by policy, state and eligibility.

spec.headline: Renting a car for the holidays? Know what follows you

entries.caption:
Flying home for the holidays and picking up a rental at the airport? Before you initial every box at the counter, it helps to know what your own policy already does. 🚗

For many personal auto policies, the coverages you carry often extend to a rental car you drive for personal use. That can include liability, and comprehensive and collision if they're on your policy, usually with the same deductibles.

A few things it may not include:
• Rental company fees, like loss of use while the car is being repaired
• Rentals for business use or outside the US and Canada
• Coverage you don't already have on your own car

Every policy is different, so a quick check before your trip can make that rental counter decision a lot easier. Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com.

Coverage varies by policy, state and eligibility.

spec.headline: New jewelry this season? Check your policy's limits
points: Theft limits on jewelry are often low

entries.caption:
Thinking about a ring, a watch or a family heirloom under the tree this year? Here's something many homeowners don't know until they need it. 💍

Most homeowners and renters policies cover jewelry as personal property, but often with a special limit for theft. That limit can be much lower than the value of a nice piece.

That's where scheduling comes in. Scheduling, sometimes called a floater or endorsement, lists a specific item on your policy at an agreed value. Depending on the policy, it may also broaden coverage to things like accidental loss.

Tips:
• Keep receipts and appraisals in a safe place
• Take clear photos of each piece
• Review values every few years, since prices change

Want to know what your policy allows for jewelry? Call (425) 419-0099 or email cody@lamensinsurance.com.

Coverage varies by policy, state and eligibility.

entries.title: Uninsured & Underinsured Motorist Coverage
entries.script: Last time, we cleared up what full coverage really means. Today, let's talk about the coverage that protects you from someone else's mistake: uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. Someone runs a red light and hits you. You're hurt, your car is damaged, and the other driver has no insurance, or only the state minimum. Their policy can't cover your medical bills or lost wages. That's where uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage can step in, helping pay for your injuries, and depending on your policy and state, damage to your car. It protects you from drivers who didn't protect you. In some states, you can decline it in writing. Here's your self-check. Is it on your policy, and do your limits match your liability limits? Next time, we'll look at how your driving habits can factor into your auto insurance. Insurance in Laymens terms.
entries.caption:
If the driver who hits you can't pay, who covers your injuries? Here's what uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is for.

entries.title: How Usage-Based Insurance Works
entries.script: Last time, we covered protection from drivers who can't pay. Today, let's talk about usage-based insurance, sometimes called telematics. Here's how it works. With your permission, a phone app or a small device can track things like how hard you brake, how fast you accelerate, how often you drive late at night, and how many miles you drive. Depending on the program and your state, that information may be used to help set your rate. Safe habits can count in your favor, and some programs look at risky habits too, so know how a program works before you sign up. It's not right for everyone, and that's okay. Here's your self-check. If someone scored your driving this week, how would you do? Next time, we'll wrap up our auto series with the coverage gaps people miss most. Insurance in Laymens terms.
